abstract: A 49-year-old woman died from metastases from a colon carcinoma. This was predominantly an ordinary tubular adenocarcinoma but it included arease of much less differentiated appearance with giant cells, while the hepatic and pulmonary metastase were poorly differentiated and contained choriocarcinoma, as established by means of morphologic and immunocytochemical examination. The choriocarcinoma appeared to be due to metaplasia within the carcinomatous tissue. This and other similar cases of mixed tumours suggest that unexpected trophoblastic differentiation may result from aberrant differentiation of locally proliferating cells, rather than originating in ectopic germ cells or in foci of embryonic totipotent cells. Implications for possible origin and for classification of tumors are briefly discussed.
abstract_ja: 49歳女性が大腸癌の転移で死亡した。原発は主として通常の管状腺癌であったが、巨細胞を伴う低分化な領域も含んでおり、肝および肺の転移巣は低分化で、形態学的および免疫細胞化学的検査により絨毛癌を含むことが確認された。絨毛癌は癌組織内の化生に起因すると考えられ、胚細胞や胚発生の全能性細胞の遺残から生じたものではないと考えられた。このような混合腫瘍の症例は、予期せぬ栄養膜分化が局所で増殖する細胞の異常な分化から生じうることを示唆しており、腫瘍の起源と分類について簡潔に考察した。
